meta.title: Inflation Isn't One Number. Here's What The CPI Actually Tracks.
meta.hook: When you hear 'inflation is 3 percent,' that number comes from tracking thousands of specific prices, not one.
meta.description: The Consumer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, tracks price changes across a fixed basket of goods and services — housing, food, transportation, medical care and more — weighted by how much a typical household actually spends on each. It's why inflation can feel different in your own life than the headline number suggests: your personal spending mix rarely matches the national average basket exactly.

scenes.narration: When you hear inflation is three percent, that number isn't tracking one price. It's tracking thousands.
